cards.name: Blend
cards.summary: Live blend between two vector objects: CorelDRAW generates a run of intermediate objects that morph shape, size, outline and colour step by step from the start object to the end object. The result is a shape tween, a stepped colour ramp, or (with many steps) a smooth 3D-tube / neon-glow look. Steps (or fixed Spacing along a path), the colour route around the colour wheel, a progressive rotation Angle and object / colour acceleration shape the run.
use_for: neon or glowing tube lettering (blend a thick dark stroke into a thin bright copy)
stepped colour ramps and op-art line patterns between two curves
morph-style shape tweens for infographics and logo explorations
evenly spaced objects along a curve (dots, chevrons, beads) with a Path and Mode = spacing
avoid: a single selected object: a blend needs a start object and an end object (the required Shape argument)
smooth photographic gradients: low Steps show visible banding; use a fountain fill or Contour instead
very high Steps on complex shapes or text: slow redraws and heavy print files
control objects with very different node structure: the in-between shapes can twist; align their start nodes first

params.name: Shape
params.does: the end object of the blend (required); the shape the method is called on is the start object
params.typical: a second shape on the page

params.name: Steps
params.does: number of intermediate objects generated between the two control objects (Mode = steps)

params.name: ColorBlendType
params.does: route the colours take: Direct goes straight from start colour to end colour; Rainbow clockwise / counter-clockwise travel around the colour wheel for rainbow in-betweens

params.name: Mode
params.does: steps = a fixed number of objects; spacing = a fixed distance between objects (meaningful on a blend attached to a Path)

params.name: Spacing
params.does: distance between intermediate objects when Mode = spacing, in document units
params.typical: 0 unless the blend runs along a path

params.name: Angle
params.does: rotation in degrees added progressively across the intermediate objects

params.name: Loop
params.does: with a non-zero Angle, swings the intermediate objects around an arc instead of only rotating them in place

params.name: Path
params.does: a curve the blend follows (blend along a path); None = straight blend

params.name: RotateShapes
params.does: on a path blend, turns every step to follow the path direction
params.typical: on for objects running along curves

params.name: SpacingAccel
params.does: object acceleration: bunches the intermediate objects toward the start or the end; 0 = even spacing
params.typical: 0; push either way to suggest speed or depth

params.name: ColorAccel
params.does: colour acceleration: makes the colour change happen faster near one end; 0 = even colour steps

params.name: AccelSize
params.does: also applies the acceleration to the size change of the steps

pairs_with: Contour, for a halo or outline around a neon blend
a Path curve (Blend along path) for objects marching along a line
Transparency on one control object for fading trails
PowerClip to confine a blend pattern inside a shape
cards.scripting: start.CreateBlend(end, 12, 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0, False, None, False, 0, 0, False)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreateBlend(Shape, Steps, ColorBlendType, Mode, Spacing, Angle, Loop, Path, RotateShapes, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, AccelSize) -> IVGEffect (apply test: effect_type 0). Demo: start = orange_box, end = blue_star of the vector plate. Menu: Effects > Blend toggles the Blend docker (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "bda9bd40-dfb8-4f1a-8cc0-651ebcccc9f7").
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live blend group; editing either control object or the blend settings regenerates the in-between steps; clearing the blend removes them, breaking it apart bakes them into plain objects
cards.cost: light; grows with Steps x node count of the control objects

review.changes: look: removed 'step and repeat' (CorelDRAW has its own Edit/Step and Repeat command, so the keyword sent searches to the wrong card). Signature, demo, status needs_input and equivalents checked against the batch and apply_tests.py: no other change.

verified.note: Listed in gallery/cdr_effect/not_rendered.json (status 'needs_input' (only current cards are rendered)), so there is no frame to check.

second_opinion.note: Agree: listed in not_rendered.json by rule (status needs_input); harness check: no render was attempted, so there is no frame to misread and the card makes no frame-based claim.

cards.name: Contour
cards.summary: Live vector effect that draws a series of evenly spaced, concentric offset copies of an object's outline, outside it, inside it, or all the way to its centre. Fill and outline colours step from the object's own colours to the chosen end colours. The result reads as topographic rings, multi-outline or inline lettering, a vector glow, or a sticker cut line.
use_for: sticker / die-cut outline around a logo or headline (1 step, Outside)
retro multi-outline and inline lettering
topographic contour-line patterns and concentric ripple backgrounds
soft vector glow: many fine steps contouring outward from the shape colour to the background colour
inset borders inside badges and buttons (Inside)
avoid: bitmaps: Contour works on vector objects; for pixels use a bitmap blur or glow
large Offset x Steps with Inside: the contours run out of room and stop early; use To Center or fewer steps
a cut line that must be edited as its own object: apply the contour, then break the contour group apart

params.name: Direction
params.does: where the contours go: Inside, Outside, or To Center (fills inward until the shape is used up, step count follows from Offset)

params.name: Offset
params.does: distance between successive contour lines, in document units; passing 0 makes the app substitute 0.15

params.name: Steps
params.does: number of contour lines for Inside / Outside
params.typical: 1 for a sticker outline, 4-10 for rings

params.name: BlendType
params.does: how fill and outline colours progress from the object to the end colours: Direct, or around the colour wheel (Rainbow clockwise / counter-clockwise)

params.name: OutlineColor
params.does: outline colour of the last contour; the in-between outlines step toward it

params.name: FillColor
params.does: fill colour of the last contour; the in-between fills step from the object fill to it
params.typical: a contrast colour for rings, the background colour for a glow

params.name: FillColor2
params.does: second end colour, used when the object has a fountain fill

params.name: SpacingAccel
params.does: bunches the contour lines toward the object or toward the last contour; 0 = even

params.name: ColorAccel
params.does: makes the colour change happen faster near one end; 0 = even

params.name: EndCapType
params.does: end shape of contours around open paths: butt, round or square

params.name: CornerType
params.does: corner shape of the contour lines: bevelled, round, or mitered variants (sharp corners that fall back to a bevel past MiterLimit)
params.typical: cdrContourCornerRound for soft rings, the mitered default for sharp lettering

params.name: MiterLimit
params.does: limit for mitered corners: corners sharper than it are bevelled (passing 0 makes the app substitute 15)

pairs_with: Blend, for neon tubes with a contour halo
Drop Shadow on the contour group for sticker mock-ups
artistic text converted to curves for clean multi-outline lettering
cards.scripting: s.CreateContour(1, 0.15, 5, 0, app.CreateRGBColor(26, 26, 26), app.CreateRGBColor(0, 194, 255), None, 0, 0, 2, 2, 15.0)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreateContour(Direction, Offset, Steps, BlendType, OutlineColor, FillColor, FillColor2, SpacingAccel, ColorAccel, EndCapType, CornerType, MiterLimit) -> IVGEffect type 6 (apply-tested; audit: all arguments omitted also works). Offset is in document units (inches in the harvest test document). Menu: Effects > Contour toggles the Contour docker (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "0a57d894-9adb-4ea7-87e3-4729eb14db54").
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live contour group linked to its control object; edit the object or the settings and the contours regenerate; clearing removes them, breaking the group apart bakes them
cards.cost: light; grows with Steps on complex outlines

review.changes: none (12-argument call, effect type 6, the 0.15 / 15 substituted defaults and the omitted-arguments audit all match the batch; demo sits inside the enums)

verified.note: Five concentric outside contour rings step from the star's blue out to the chosen cyan (#00C2FF) around the star, a vector glow / sticker-outline look as described.

cards.name: Envelope
cards.summary: Live vector distortion that wraps an object (shapes, artistic text, groups) in an editable envelope outline so its contents bend to fit: arches, bulges, waves or any custom outline. From a script, CreateEnvelope applies one of the Envelope docker's preset outlines by index; CreateEnvelopeFromShape / FromCurve copy the outline of another shape or curve to fit artwork into it.
use_for: arched or bulging headline text for badges, labels and signage
fitting a word or logo into a shape (shield, circle, banner) with CreateEnvelopeFromShape
waving flag or ribbon distortion of vector art
squeezed / stretched packaging and sticker type
avoid: photos: the harvest lists a vector object as the requirement and bitmap support was not probed; for a pixel image test first, or use a bitmap distortion
straight-line one- or two-point perspective: use Add Perspective
small text under strong envelopes: it becomes illegible; keep distortion gentle
PresetIndex 1 or 2: on the 2026-10 renders they returned an envelope effect but changed nothing visible (0.005 mean px on the star); use 3-6

params.name: PresetIndex
params.does: which preset envelope outline to apply (index into the Envelope docker's preset list); the Envelope Preset Library render (gallery/cdr_preset/bd38895dce0b.png) shows 1 and 2 leave a square unchanged, 3 maps it to a circle, 4 to a pinched-waist shape, 5 and 6 to slanted parallelograms; the docker's names for them are not mapped
params.typical: 3 (circle) or 4 to 6; 1 and 2 give no visible change

params.name: Mode
params.does: mapping mode, how the contents follow the envelope: Putty (smoothest, maps the corners), Original, Horizontal or Vertical (fit along one axis first)

params.name: KeepLines
params.does: keeps straight segments straight instead of bending them into curves

pairs_with: artistic text, for arched titles
Extrude after the envelope for bent 3D lettering
a frame shape as the source of CreateEnvelopeFromShape
cards.scripting: s.CreateEnvelope(3, 2, False)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreateEnvelope(PresetIndex, Mode, KeepLines) -> IVGEffect type 2 (apply-tested). Fit into another shape: s.CreateEnvelopeFromShape(frame, 2, False, 1). Menu: Effects > Envelope toggles the Envelope docker (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "e08bc376-0809-4f3b-a001-7869f02fd74c").
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live envelope, re-editable with the Envelope tool's nodes; clearing the envelope restores the original object

review.changes: avoid: 'envelopes distort vector objects' stated bitmap exclusion as fact; the batch only gives requires = vector object, so it is now marked as not probed. Calls, Mode enum and the apply-tested PresetIndex 1 match the batch.

verified.note: New frame (PresetIndex 3, Mode 2): the star's straight edges are bent into curves, its arms bowed and its outline pulled toward a rounded envelope, while the box, circle, type and zigzag are untouched: the live envelope distortion described.

previous.note: No frame: failed.json says star.CreateEnvelope(1, 2, False) returned an effect but changed the page by only 0.0051 mean px; the demo is the cause: the Envelope Preset Library render (gallery/cdr_preset/bd38895dce0b.png) shows PresetIndex 1 and 2 leave a checker square unchanged while 3 maps it to a circle, so the demo now uses PresetIndex 3.

second_opinion.note: Harness check: the renderer did apply CreateEnvelope (effect type 2 returned) and failed only the 0.05 visibility rule, so the demo is the cause; the preset-library frame (gallery/cdr_preset/bd38895dce0b.png) shows index 3 maps a checker square to a circle, so PresetIndex 3 (inside the int type, no harvested range) should pass the rule on the star.

cards.name: Extrude
cards.summary: Live vector 3D effect that projects an object's outline toward (or away from) a vanishing point and builds solid side faces, so flat shapes and text become blocky 3D letters and objects. Side faces take the object's own fill, a solid colour or a two-colour shade, and an optional bevel can chamfer the front face.
use_for: retro 3D block lettering for posters and titles
isometric-style icons and signs (parallel extrusion)
chunky 3D logo marks for print where everything must stay vector
solid long shadows (Back Parallel with a solid dark fill): the scriptable stand-in for the Block Shadow tool, which has no object-model call
avoid: photoreal 3D with materials and textures: Extrude builds vector faces coloured by the Shading setting, plus optional light sources (EffectExtrude.SetLight in the cdr_api harvest), not rendered materials
bitmaps: vector objects only
small text with a deep extrusion: the faces collide and get illegible; lower Depth
very complex shapes or long text: many faces, slow redraws and heavy files

params.name: Type
params.does: extrusion style: Small / Big Back or Front run toward or away from the vanishing point in perspective; Back / Front Parallel keep the depth edges parallel (no taper)
params.typical: cdrExtrudeSmallBack for classic 3D type, cdrExtrudeBackParallel for isometric or long shadows

params.name: VPType
params.does: what the vanishing point is locked to: the shape, the page, or shared between several extrusions

params.name: VPX
params.does: x of the vanishing point, in document units
params.typical: outside the object, to the side the depth should go

params.name: VPY
params.does: y of the vanishing point, in document units

params.name: Depth
params.does: how far the extrusion runs toward the vanishing point

params.name: Shading
params.does: side-face colouring: Object fill (same as the front), Solid fill (BaseColor), Color shading (BaseColor to ShadingColor gradient)

params.name: BaseColor
params.does: the solid side colour, or the near colour of colour shading
params.typical: a mid tone of the object colour

params.name: ShadingColor
params.does: the far colour of colour shading

params.name: BevelDepth
params.does: size of a bevel cut around the front face; 0 = no bevel
params.typical: 0, or small for a chiselled edge

params.name: BevelAngle
params.does: slope of the bevel in degrees

params.name: BevelColor
params.does: colour of the bevel faces
params.typical: a lighter tone of the object colour

params.name: BevelOnly
params.does: show only the bevel and hide the extruded depth

pairs_with: Envelope first, for bent 3D lettering
Contour on the front face for an outlined 3D title
Drop Shadow under the extrude group to ground it
cards.scripting: s.CreateExtrude(0, 0, 12.0, 2.0, 40.0, 2, app.CreateRGBColor(110, 110, 110), app.CreateRGBColor(17, 17, 17), 0.0, 45.0, None, False)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreateExtrude(Type, VPType, VPX, VPY, Depth, Shading, BaseColor, ShadingColor, BevelDepth, BevelAngle, BevelColor, BevelOnly) -> IVGEffect type 1 (apply-tested). VPX / VPY are document units; the demo values assume the imported plate spans about 20 x 11.25 in from the page origin, so move them if the plate sits elsewhere, and keep the point outside the target shape (with that layout and CorelDRAW's bottom-left origin, (12, 2) sits against the right end of the PGD type, so extrude orange_box, blue_star or grad_circle, not the type). Bevel afterwards: EffectExtrude.SetBevel(Depth, Angle, ShowBevelOnly). Menu: Effects > Extrude toggles the Extrude docker (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "952e4cc8-4316-4bca-9ad9-9f79cf8574f2").
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live extrude group; depth, vanishing point and shading stay editable; clearing removes it, breaking the group apart bakes the faces into objects
cards.cost: moderate: many faces on text or detailed outlines

review.changes: avoid: 'Extrude is flat vector shading' was wrong, since IVGEffectExtrude has LightPresent / SetLight / LightIntensity in the cdr_api harvest; now says vector faces plus optional lights, no materials. use_for: long-shadow line now points at Block Shadow. scripting: the vanishing point must sit outside the target, and (12, 2) sits against the PGD type with the assumed plate layout.

verified.note: The star is extruded into a solid 3D block toward a vanishing point to the right: grey side faces shaded from #6E6E6E to near black run behind the star and the gradient circle, retro 3D type style.

cards.name: Lens
cards.summary: Effects > Lens turns a closed vector shape into a live lens: whatever lies under the shape's area (vectors and bitmaps; on the 2026-10 renders the Invert lens recoloured both the photo and the shapes under it, while Fish Eye at -100 warped only the vector shapes and left the photo nearly unchanged) is shown through a filter (Magnify, Fish Eye, Wireframe, Color Limit, Color Add, Invert, Brighten, Tinted Grayscale, Heat Map, Transparency or Custom Color Map) while the objects underneath stay unchanged. This card covers the Lens docker and the CreateLens call as a whole; each lens type also has its own card.
use_for: magnifier call-outs on maps, diagrams and product details (Magnify, Fish Eye)
tinted or monochrome panels over part of a photo to back text (Tinted Grayscale, Transparency)
inverted or heat-map bands for graphic posters
x-ray / wireframe reveal of the artwork under a shape (Wireframe)
avoid: an open path or a bitmap as the lens object: the lens must be a closed vector shape
artwork handed to other apps: lenses are a CorelDRAW live effect; freeze or flatten the result before export
global colour correction of a whole photo: use a bitmap adjustment instead of a page-sized lens

params.name: Type
params.does: which lens to make (see enum_labels)

params.name: RateOrMagnification
params.does: strength: the magnification factor for Magnify, a rate in percent for Fish Eye and the colour / transparency lenses

params.name: Color1
params.does: the lens colour for the colour lenses (Color Limit, Color Add, Tinted Grayscale, Transparency) and the start colour of a Custom Color Map

params.name: Color2
params.does: second colour for lens types that use two (end colour of a Custom Color Map); exact use per type not harvested

params.name: ColorMapPalette
params.does: how a Custom Color Map runs from Color1 to Color2: Direct, or around the colour wheel

pairs_with: an ellipse or rounded rectangle as the lens shape over a photo or diagram
PowerClip, to keep a lens inside a frame
Transparency lens plus Tinted Grayscale for a text panel over busy photos
cards.scripting: lensShape.CreateLens(1, -100.0, None, None, 0)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreateLens(Type, RateOrMagnification, Color1, Color2, ColorMapPalette) -> IVGEffect. lensShape = a new closed shape (e.g. an ellipse) drawn on top of the vector plate so it straddles orange_box, blue_star and some empty page: a lens only shows what lies under it, so applied to a plate shape that sits on blank page it just looks like a recoloured shape. Menu: Effects > Lens toggles the Lens docker (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "1c86e69f-30a5-4a01-85cb-e4a76cca5fd5").
cards.non_destructive: yes: the objects under the lens are untouched; moving or reshaping the lens changes what it affects; removing the lens restores the view
cards.cost: light for colour lenses; Magnify / Fish Eye over complex artwork redraw slowly

review.changes: scripting: the lens shape was placed 'above the vector shapes and the photo', but the CorelDRAW vector plate has no photo. It now says to draw a new shape that straddles orange_box, blue_star and empty page, because a lens over blank page reads as a plain recolour. Call, enums and the per-type sibling cards (lens:cdrLens*) checked.

verified.note: New demo, Fish Eye at rate -100 (a negative fish eye, a pinch): inside the lens circle the vector shapes are pulled toward its centre and bent (the orange box's edges curve, the zigzag is displaced into a bent copy) while the photo half under the lens barely changes (1-3 % of its pixels by more than 16 levels); outside the circle nothing changes: a live lens over what lies beneath, as described; summary notes the photo case.

previous.note: The frame shows a lens circle over the photo and shapes inverting what lies beneath it, which is what the card describes; but Type 5 is Invert, so the frame is byte-identical to the Invert lens card's frame and adds nothing; demo changed to Type 1 (Fish Eye) at rate -100 to show the docker's other side (a negative fish-eye pinch, a claim no other lens frame tests).

second_opinion.note: Checked the demo change: Type 1 = Fish Eye in enum_labels, rate -100 is a pinch no other lens card renders (Fish Eye uses +300), and the old frame is byte-identical to the Invert lens frame (live chain pixel audit), so the duplicate was the card's demo, not the renderer.

cards.name: Add Perspective
cards.summary: Puts an editable four-corner perspective grid on a vector object or group so the artwork recedes toward one or two vanishing points, like a sign or wall seen at an angle. Interactively you drag the grid's corner nodes; from a script you give the vanishing points. The object stays live, and the perspective can be edited or cleared later.
use_for: placing a flat logo or label on a receding wall, box side or billboard mock-up
receding title text (one-point perspective)
quick vector packaging and signage views
floor, road or grid patterns running to a horizon
avoid: photos: the harvest lists a vector object or group as the requirement and bitmap support was not probed; for a pixel image test first, or use Photoshop Edit/Transform/Perspective
true depth with side faces: use Extrude
curved bends rather than straight-line perspective: use Envelope

params.name: HorizVanishPointX
params.does: x of the horizontal vanishing point (optional variant, document units)
params.typical: well to one side of the object

params.name: HorizVanishPointY
params.does: y of the horizontal vanishing point
params.typical: near the object's vertical centre for an eye-level view

params.name: VertVanishPointX
params.does: x of the vertical vanishing point; leave both vertical values out for one-point perspective

params.name: VertVanishPointY
params.does: y of the vertical vanishing point (far above or below for a looking-up / looking-down view)

pairs_with: a group of logo + text, so the whole layout recedes together
Extrude after perspective for deeper 3D signage
Drop Shadow to seat the angled object on the page
cards.scripting: s.CreatePerspective(8.0, 5.0)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.CreatePerspective(HorizVanishPointX, HorizVanishPointY, VertVanishPointX, VertVanishPointY) -> IVGEffect type 8 (apply-tested with only the horizontal point = one-point perspective); pass all four values for two-point perspective. (8.0, 5.0) suited the apply test's 1.2 x 0.9 in rectangle at x = 1 in; on the vector plate (about 20 x 11.25 in, bottom-left origin) that point falls in the narrow gap between orange_box and blue_star, so choose a vanishing point well clear of the target, e.g. far to its right at about its vertical centre. The params are variants (harvest type unknown), so no demo_settings are given. Menu: Object > Perspective > Add Perspective (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "00f16820-b826-45a2-ad9a-4287b280a7b2").
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live perspective effect; the grid nodes stay editable and clearing the perspective restores the flat object

review.changes: avoid: the bitmap exclusion was stated as fact; the batch only gives requires = vector object or group, so it is now marked as not probed. scripting: the apply-test point (8.0, 5.0) falls between orange_box and blue_star on the plate, so it now says to pick a point well clear of the target. Leaving demo_settings out stays right, because the params are variant (type unknown).

verified.note: One-point perspective toward a vanishing point at the right: the star's right side shrinks and recedes (top point leans right, right arms shorter), a sign-seen-at-an-angle look; moderate but clear against ref_vector.

cards.name: PowerClip
cards.summary: Places one object (a photo, artwork or text) inside another closed object that acts as a frame, so the content shows only within the frame's outline: CorelDRAW's clipping mask. The content stays whole and can be repositioned inside the frame or extracted later.
use_for: photo inside headline lettering or a logo shape
images cropped into circles, blobs or badges for social graphics
patterns or textures masked to a shape
keeping artwork inside a trim or bleed frame
avoid: a single object: it needs content plus a container
an open path as the frame: use a closed shape or artistic text
feathered or faded edges: PowerClip is a hard clip; add Transparency to the contents or frame for soft fades
very large bitmaps in many frames: file size balloons; crop or resample the bitmap first

params.name: Shape
params.does: the container (frame) object; the method is called on the content shape
params.typical: a closed shape or artistic text

params.name: CenterInContainer
params.does: cdrTrue centres the content in the frame, cdrFalse keeps its current position; cdrUndefined (the default) presumably defers to the app's own PowerClip centring preference (only the label was harvested)

pairs_with: artistic text in a heavy font as the frame
Contour or an outline on the frame to edge the clipped image
Transparency on the contents for a tinted photo-in-type look
cards.scripting: photo.AddToPowerClip(star, -1)  # Python/pywin32; Shape.AddToPowerClip(Shape=container, CenterInContainer) -> void, called on the CONTENT (apply test: content placed into a container, container.PowerClip.Shapes.Count = 1). Demo: plate_photo.png bitmap into the blue_star (or the PGD type). Menu: Object > PowerClip > Place Inside Frame (FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "da1efe7f-16d0-459b-94b2-836a6b5e6bc6").
cards.non_destructive: yes: the content is kept intact inside the frame and can be edited, moved or extracted again

review.changes: params / enum_labels: cdrUndefined 'follows the app's PowerClip option' was stated as fact; only the label was harvested, so it is now marked as presumed and as the default (-2). Call direction (content.AddToPowerClip(container)) checked against apply_tests.py, and needs_input is right.

verified.note: Listed in gallery/cdr_effect/not_rendered.json (status 'needs_input' (only current cards are rendered)), so there is no frame to check.

second_opinion.note: Agree: listed in not_rendered.json by rule (status needs_input); harness check: no render was attempted, so there is no frame to misread and the card makes no frame-based claim.

cards.name: Block Shadow
cards.summary: Toolbox tool: drag from an object to add a solid, hard-edged vector block (a 'long shadow') that runs from its outline in one direction, one flat colour with no blur or gradient, as used in flat-design icons and retro type. Its settings live on the tool's property bar and were not probed; there is no scripting member for it.
use_for: flat-design long shadows on icons and app tiles
retro solid offset shadows behind lettering
vinyl-cut or screen-print output where the shadow must be one solid vector shape
avoid: soft, blurred shadows: use the Drop Shadow tool
automated pipelines: no VGCore member applies it (harvest error); a script can only select the tool. Approximate it with Extrude (Back Parallel, solid fill) instead
photographic shadows that should fade with distance: use Drop Shadow or a Blend to the background colour
pairs_with: flat icon shapes and bold display type
a background colour one step darker than the shadow for a layered flat look
cards.scripting: No apply call: VGCoreAuto.tlb 25.1 has no Block Shadow member (harvest error). FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "249b7791-6d54-401b-a326-378c53773a52" only selects the tool; the shadow must then be dragged by hand. Scripted stand-in: s.CreateExtrude(4, 0, vpx, vpy, depth, 1, darkColor, None, 0.0, 45.0, None, False) (Back Parallel, solid fill) gives a similar solid block.
cards.non_destructive: not harvested: whether the block stays linked to its object was not probed

review.changes: none (scriptable no and the InvokeItem GUID match the batch error; no params, so no demo_settings; empty equivalents are right because neither Illustrator nor Photoshop has a solid block-shadow command)

verified.note: Listed in gallery/cdr_effect/not_rendered.json (scriptable 'no': No apply call: VGCoreAuto.tlb 25.1 has no Block Shadow member (harvest error). FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "249b7791-6d54-401b-a326-378c53773a52" only selects the tool; the shadow must then be dragged by hand. Scripted stand-in: [...]), so there is no frame to check. Harness check: there is no apply call to test, so the card's look is unverified, not wrong.

second_opinion.note: Agree: listed in not_rendered.json by rule (no scripted apply call); harness check: no render was attempted, so there is no frame to misread and the card makes no frame-based claim.

cards.name: Push & Pull
cards.summary: Distort tool in Push & Pull mode: a live vector distortion that moves an object's segments in or out relative to a centre point. Depending on the sign and size of Amplitude, ordinary shapes become spiky star-like forms or puffy, petal-like flower forms. It works best on shapes with several nodes.
use_for: starburst / sale-badge shapes from a circle or polygon
flower and petal motifs from simple polygons
playful pinched or bloated logo and lettering explorations
organic blob shapes for backgrounds
avoid: shapes with very few nodes (a plain rectangle) give crude lobes: start from a polygon or add nodes
bitmaps: vector objects only
precise geometry: the result is free-form; convert to curves before node editing

params.name: OriginX
params.does: x of the distortion centre, in document units

params.name: OriginY

cards.name: Twister
cards.summary: Distort tool in Twister mode: a live vector distortion that rotates an object's outline around a centre point so its edges sweep into a spiral swirl. Angle sets how far it twists; the property bar splits it into whole rotations plus extra degrees. Curly results need enough nodes, so it shows best on stars, polygons and text.
use_for: swirl, vortex and hypnotic spiral motifs
twisted star and flower ornaments
warped logo and lettering explorations
tornado or whirlpool icon shapes
avoid: simple shapes with few nodes: a rectangle barely curls; use a star or add nodes
readable text: more than a small twist destroys legibility
bitmaps: vector only; for pixels use a bitmap swirl / twirl filter

params.name: OriginX

params.does: y of the twist centre, in document units

params.name: Angle
params.does: twist amount in degrees; the sign sets the direction (which sign is clockwise was not harvested)

pairs_with: a Star or Polygon with many points as the starting shape
Push & Pull first, then Twister, for swirled flowers
Blend between a twisted and an untwisted copy for a spiralling tunnel
